question: A huge system of billions of stars and cloud of dust and gases is known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Galaxy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A galaxy is a massive, gravitationally bound system that consists of stars, stellar remnants, interstellar gas, dust, and dark matter.
 
• The term galaxy is derived from the Greek word "galaxias," which means "milky," a reference to the Milky Way galaxy.
 
• Galaxies can contain billions or even trillions of stars and can range in size from a few thousand to several hundred thousand light-years in diameter.
 
• There are various types of galaxies, including spiral galaxies, elliptical galaxies, and irregular galaxies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Universe**

 
 
• The Universe encompasses all of space and time, and contains all of the galaxies, stars, and planets.
 
• It is believed to have begun with the Big Bang approximately 13.8 billion years ago.
 
• It is constantly expanding, and its vastness is beyond human comprehension.
 
 
 
• **World**
 
 
• The term "world" usually refers to the Earth and all life on it.
 
• It can also be used to denote a particular area or domain, such as the "world of science" or "world of music".
 
 
 
• **Constellation**
 
 
• A constellation is a group of stars that forms a recognizable pattern in the night sky.
 
• These patterns are often named after mythological figures, animals, or objects.
 
• There are 88 recognized constellations in modern astronomy.
